Read GlyPep-Quant label-free quantification results

read_glyco_decipher_glypep_quant.Rd

Import a GlyPep-Quant CSV produced from Glyco-Decipher or pGlyco3 identifications. read_glyco_decipher_glypep_quant() extracts protein coordinates from Glyco-Decipher glycopeptide labels such as Q86XS8@135;. read_pglyco3_glypep_quant() reads pGlyco3 glycopeptide accessions such as Q86XS8 and records their unreported protein sites as NA.

Usage

read_glyco_decipher_glypep_quant(
  fp,
  sample_info = NULL,
  quant_method = "label-free",
  glycan_type = "N",
  sample_name_converter = NULL,
  orgdb = "org.Hs.eg.db"
)

read_pglyco3_glypep_quant(
  fp,
  sample_info = NULL,
  quant_method = "label-free",
  glycan_type = "N",
  sample_name_converter = NULL,
  orgdb = "org.Hs.eg.db"
)

Arguments

fp

Local path or HTTP(S) URL of the result file.

sample_info

Local path or HTTP(S) URL of the sample information CSV, or a sample information data.frame/tibble.

quant_method

Quantification method. Only "label-free" is supported.

glycan_type

Glycan type. One of "N", "O-GalNAc", "O-GlcNAc", "O-Man", "O-Fuc", or "O-Glc". Default is "N".

sample_name_converter

A function to convert sample names from file paths. The function should take a character vector of old sample names and return new sample names. Note that sample names in sample_info should match the new names. If NULL, original names are kept.

orgdb

name of the OrgDb package to use for UniProt to gene symbol conversion. Default is "org.Hs.eg.db".

Value

A glyexp::GlycoproteomicSE() with one row per input record. Row metadata include the inferred leader protein, the candidate accessions in protein_group, and protein_site (an integer, or NA for absent or ambiguous coordinates). reported_glycan retains the original label, including any mass shift, alongside glycan_composition. Site tables retain reported_site. Glycopeptide tables retain the original reported_protein and reported_peptide labels and provide the unmodified sequence in peptide.

Details

Both readers recognize the summary format from its column headers.

  • site.csv reports a site-specific glycan per row in Site and Glycan.

  • glycopeptide.csv reports a glycopeptide per row in Peptide, Glycan, and Protein.

All remaining columns contain sample abundances. Empty cells and zeros become NA. Rows are retained in file order, including distinct modified forms of the same peptide or glycan.

See also

Published GlyPep-Quant result files (PXD057799)

Examples

fp <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
writeLines(c("Peptide,Glycan,Protein,HeLa_01",
             "AAFHNAVAVVIYNNK,Hex(8)HexNAc(2),Q86XS8@135;,831800"), fp)
se <- read_glyco_decipher_glypep_quant(fp)
#> ℹ Reading data
#> ℹ No sample information file passed in. An empty tibble will be used.
#> ℹ Reading data

#> ℹ Package `org.Hs.eg.db` not installed. Skipping gene symbol conversion.
#> ℹ Reading data

#> ✔ Reading data [277ms]
#> 
writeLines(c("Peptide,Glycan,Protein,HeLa_01",
             "AAFHNAVAVVIYNNK,Hex(8)HexNAc(2),Q86XS8,831800"), fp)
se <- read_pglyco3_glypep_quant(fp)
#> ℹ Reading data
#> ℹ No sample information file passed in. An empty tibble will be used.
#> ℹ Reading data

#> ℹ Package `org.Hs.eg.db` not installed. Skipping gene symbol conversion.
#> ℹ Reading data

#> ✔ Reading data [39ms]
#> 
unlink(fp)
